title: The State of American AI, October 2026
notice: Independent project. Not a United States government website. Every figure counts published records in the USASI catalog as of the data cutoff; coverage is selective, so counts are not a census, a ranking, or a measure of capability.

tables.title: Organization records by ownership
tables.caption: Ownership category of each of the 150 organization records.
tables.counted: Each published organization record has exactly one ownership category, recorded from its sources: publicly traded, privately held, nonprofit, a unit of another organization, foundation-hosted, a public institution, or unknown. Research units and subsidiaries have their own records. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Independent organizations and units
tables.caption: Organization records that stand alone, and records for a unit of another organization in the catalog.
tables.counted: A unit is a research unit, division, subsidiary, or hosted project whose record names a parent organization. Units are counted separately so that a parent and its unit are never presented as two independent companies. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: What the organizations do
tables.caption: Documented roles on organization records, such as model developer or chip designer.
tables.counted: Roles are the documented activities recorded for each organization. Most records have more than one role, so the rows add up to more than the 150 records; each share is out of all organization records.

tables.title: Sectors
tables.caption: Sector tags on organization records.
tables.counted: Sectors are applied only where a record's evidence supports them, and a record can have several, so rows add up to more than the 150 records. Records with no sector tag are counted in their own row.

tables.title: Headquarters by U.S. state
tables.caption: Organization records by the U.S. state named in their documented headquarters.
tables.counted: The state is read only from the text of each record's sourced headquarters label (for example “Santa Clara, California”). Offices, data centers, and other locations are not counted. Records whose label names no U.S. state are counted in the last row. Each record counts once; rows add up to the total.

rows.label: No U.S. state in the headquarters label

tables.title: Founded, by decade
tables.caption: Organization records by the decade of their documented founding year.
tables.counted: Founding years come from each record's sourced founding date. Records with no founding year recorded are counted in the last row: a missing year means the catalog has not documented it, not that the organization is new. Units are counted separately from their parents. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Open Models & Tools records by kind
tables.caption: All 270 published records in the Open Models & Tools directory, by kind.
tables.counted: Model families (overview records for a line of models) are counted separately from model releases (one record per assessed release, which carries the license and checklist). Frameworks, runtimes, and research stacks together are this report's software. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Model releases by openness tier
tables.caption: The openness tier of each of the 96 model releases under USASI rubric v0.2.
tables.counted: Tiers are computed from each release's public-materials checklist and licenses under USASI rubric v0.2; they are never typed by hand. Each release has exactly one tier, so rows add up to the total. In the rubric the open tiers are cumulative (every open-stack release is also open-weight), so open-weight in the wider sense is the first three rows together: 90 releases.

tables.title: Can the weights be downloaded?
tables.caption: Model releases by the documented availability of their weights.
tables.counted: From the weights entry of each release's checklist. Public download: the general public can download the parameters (license terms may still restrict use). Gated: available only by request, with approval, or to some users. Not public: documented as unavailable. Not assessed: the evidence is missing or insufficient. Rows add up to the total.

rows.label: Gated (by request, approval, or for some users)

tables.title: Model releases by documented release quarter
tables.caption: Model releases by the calendar quarter of their documented release date.
tables.counted: The quarter of each release's documented release date. Dates documented only as a year cannot be placed in a quarter and are counted separately, as are releases with no documented date. The catalog records a few assessed releases per model family, mostly recent ones chosen when the family was researched, so this shows the catalog's coverage over time, not how often models are released. The last quarter is partial: it runs to the data cutoff. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Organizations with open-weight releases in the catalog
tables.caption: Organization records by the number of open-weight model releases (of 90) that list them.
tables.counted: Open-weight releases (the open-weight tier or a higher one) counted for each organization record the release lists. A release that lists two organizations counts for both, so rows can add up to more than the total. Counts reflect the releases this catalog has assessed, not everything an organization has published.

tables.title: License family of the weights
tables.caption: Model releases by the kind of license that applies to their weights.
tables.counted: Licenses that apply to a release's weights (weights, weights and code, or everything). Standard permissive: an SPDX identifier on this report's permissive list (Apache-2.0, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, NCSA, Zlib, BSL-1.0, 0BSD, Unlicense, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, ODC-By-1.0, PDDL-1.0, CDLA-Permissive-2.0). Standard copyleft: a GPL-family, MPL, EPL, or share-alike identifier. Non-commercial: the license's guide on this site is in the non-commercial category, or its SPDX identifier or name says non-commercial. Custom: any other license, usually the publisher's own terms without an SPDX identifier. A release with several weights licenses counts once, in its most restrictive family (non-commercial, then custom, then copyleft, then permissive). Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Licenses on model weights
tables.caption: The licenses that apply to model releases' weights, by how many releases use each.
tables.counted: Each license that applies to a release's weights, grouped by this site's license guide when one matches and otherwise by SPDX identifier or recorded name. A release counts once per license; a release with two weights licenses counts under both.

tables.title: Licenses on software
tables.caption: The code licenses of the 95 framework, runtime, and research-stack records.
tables.counted: Each license that applies to a project's code, grouped by license guide, SPDX identifier, or recorded name. Projects often license different parts differently, so a project can count under several licenses and rows add up to more than the total.

tables.title: Documented configurations by where they run
tables.caption: The 29 configurations in the finder, by where the model runs.
tables.counted: A configuration is one documented way to do a task: a specific combination of model, runtime, app, or hosted service, with requirements restated from the publisher's own documentation. Local: runs on your own computer. Hybrid: a tool on your computer that sends requests to a hosted model. Hosted: runs on the provider's servers. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Memory the publisher documents
tables.caption: The 21 local configurations by the memory figure their publisher states.
tables.counted: The publisher's own memory statement for the exact variant named on each configuration, as recorded with its source. Graphics-memory (VRAM) and system-memory figures are kept apart, because they describe different memory. A figure is the publisher's estimate, not a USASI test, unless the record documents a test. Configurations without a stated figure are counted in the last row. Rows add up to the total.

rows.label: Graphics memory (VRAM): more than 8, up to 16 GB
System memory: more than 8, up to 16 GB

tables.title: Configurations that fit each amount of memory
tables.caption: How many local configurations fit each amount of graphics memory or Apple silicon unified memory.
tables.counted: The same rule as the Local AI by memory pages: a configuration is listed when every finder requirement is met and the publisher's figure is within the amount. A configuration that fits 8 GB also fits larger amounts, so rows overlap; shares are out of all local configurations.

tables.title: Current job listings by location
tables.caption: The 7,305 current listings by where their locations are.
tables.counted: Listings from employers' own job feeds that were open and confirmed within 48 hours of the snapshot time, the Jobs directory's default view. Applications are on employers' sites; job data are refreshed daily, so these counts are frozen with the edition. Locations are read from the employer's text without geocoding. U.S. locations only: names the United States or a U.S. state and no place outside it. U.S. and elsewhere: names both. Outside the U.S. only: names only places outside it. Not determinable: gives nothing the rules can place (for example a city without a state). Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Current job listings naming each U.S. state
tables.caption: Current listings with a location that names each U.S. state.
tables.counted: A listing counts in a state when one of its employer-supplied locations names it: a postal code after a city (“Atlanta, GA”), the full state name, “New York City” or “NYC”, or “Washington, DC”. This is the rule of the Jobs by state pages. A listing that names several states counts in each, and listings that also name places outside the U.S. are included, so rows overlap. Locations that give only a city or only the country name no state and are not counted here.

tables.title: Current job listings by employer
tables.caption: Current listings by the organization whose job feed published them (64 employers).
tables.counted: Each listing counts once, for the organization whose official job feed published it. Only organizations whose feed the site reads are included. Counts describe open postings at one moment, not company size, growth, or hiring trends. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Remote job listings
tables.caption: Current listings that are remote, and whether a remote listing names only U.S. places.
tables.counted: Remote: the employer marks the workplace as remote, or a listed location says “Remote” (for example “Remote - US”). Remote, U.S. locations only: also names only U.S. places, the rule of the Remote jobs, U.S. locations page. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Policy tracker documents by type
tables.caption: The 30 U.S. federal AI policy documents in the tracker, by document type.
tables.counted: Each published document in the policy tracker, by its document type as recorded from the official text. Types with no document are shown as zero. Rows add up to the total.

tables.title: Policy tracker documents by status
tables.caption: Tracked documents by their status at their last review.
tables.counted: Status as recorded from official sources when the document was last reviewed: in effect, final, revoked, superseded, rescinded, draft, or status not stated. A revoked or superseded document stays in the tracker with that status. Rows add up to the total.

findings.text: Of 150 organization records, 95 (63%) have a documented headquarters in California; headquarters labels name 18 states and Washington, D.C. in all.
findings.definition: Organization records: published records in Companies & Labs, research units included. The state is read only from each record's sourced headquarters label.

findings.text: 90 of 96 model releases (94%) have weights the public can download; 6 are gated, and none is recorded as not public.
findings.definition: Model releases: one record per assessed release. Weights the public can download: the open-weight tier or a higher one under USASI rubric v0.2; license terms may still restrict use.

findings.text: 56 of 96 model releases (58%) license their weights under a standard permissive license such as Apache-2.0 or MIT; 34 (35%) use a custom license and 4 (4%) carry non-commercial terms.
findings.definition: License family of the license that applies to each release's weights; a release with several weights licenses counts in its most restrictive family. Non-commercial is counted only where the license's guide, SPDX identifier, or name says so.

findings.text: 21 of 29 documented configurations run on your own computer; 17 of those state a publisher memory figure, from 2 GB to 26 GB.
findings.definition: Configurations: the finder's documented combinations of model, runtime, app, or service. Memory figure: the publisher's own statement for the named variant, not a USASI test.

findings.text: 7,305 job listings from 64 employers were current at the snapshot; 9% are marked remote, and 70% list U.S. locations only.
findings.definition: Current: open in the employer's own job feed and confirmed within 48 hours of the snapshot. Remote: marked remote by the employer or with a location that says “Remote”.
